Vaccines in Special Populations

live vaccines by CD4 count in HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) · extra vaccines by condition · HIV additions · hepatitis B serologyIs it live, and which defense has the condition removed?

Bottom line
  • Two checks decide most cases: whether the vaccine is live, and which defense the condition has removed.
  • In HIV (human immunodeficiency virus), live MMR (measles, mumps and rubella) and varicella need a CD4 (cluster of differentiation 4) count of 200 or higher (MMR also a CD4 percentage of 15% or higher for 6 months); LAIV (live attenuated influenza vaccine) is never given; vaccines that are not live, including recombinant zoster, go at any CD4 count.
  • Asplenia: pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b); complement deficiency or eculizumab: meningococcal; cirrhosis: pneumococcal, hepatitis A and B; pregnancy: no MMR, varicella or LAIV.

Live vaccines can revert to a virulent form, so they are usually withheld in severe immunodeficiency (in HIV, a CD4 count under 200) and in pregnancy; inactivated vaccines follow the routine schedule, and each condition adds the vaccines its lost defense calls for.

Vaccines in HIV by CD4 count
VaccineCD4 under 200CD4 200 or higher
MMRContraindicatedGive once the CD4 percentage has also been 15% or higher for at least 6 months
VaricellaContraindicatedGive The combined MMRV (measles, mumps, rubella and varicella) vaccine is not used in HIV at any severity; use the single-antigen varicella vaccine.
Yellow feverContraindicatedGive with caution
Live attenuated influenza (LAIV)NeverNever: inactivated influenza instead
BCG (bacille Calmette-Guérin) and oral polioNeverNever
Recombinant zoster The old live zoster vaccine was discontinued in 2020; only the recombinant vaccine is in use.GiveGive
Extra vaccines by condition
ConditionExtra vaccines
HIVPneumococcal, meningococcal ACWY (serogroups A, C, W and Y), hepatitis A and B, recombinant zoster, HPV, yearly inactivated influenza (next table)
Cirrhosis or other chronic liver diseasePneumococcal; hepatitis A and B The liver makes complement, so cirrhosis loses opsonins; portosystemic shunting bypasses the Kupffer cells; hepatitis A on a cirrhotic liver can be fulminant.
Asplenia, splenectomy or sickle cell disease (functional asplenia)Pneumococcal, meningococcal ACWY and B, Hib; before a planned splenectomy when possible Without splenic phagocytes, encapsulated organisms cause overwhelming bacteremia: pneumococcus, meningococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b (SHiN: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, N. meningitidis).
Complement deficiency or eculizumabMeningococcal ACWY and B Eculizumab blocks C5; the terminal components, C5 through C9, form the membrane attack complex that kills Neisseria.
Cerebrospinal fluid leak or cochlear implantPneumococcal Both give pneumococcus direct access to the meninges.
PregnancyTdap (tetanus, diphtheria and acellular pertussis) in every pregnancy, at 27 to 36 weeks, and inactivated influenza; no MMR, varicella or LAIV
HIV additions to the adult schedule
VaccineRule in HIV
PneumococcalAt any age and any CD4 count, soon after diagnosis
Meningococcal ACWY2 doses at least 8 weeks apart, then a booster every 5 years while risk remains; the same schedule as asplenia, complement deficiency and complement-inhibitor use
Hepatitis A and BUnless immune (hepatitis B: serology table below); HIV makes hepatitis A more severe
Recombinant zosterFrom age 19 rather than 50; not live, so permitted at a low CD4 count
HPV (human papillomavirus)Through age 26; 27 to 45 by shared decision; within those ages, HIV gets the 3-dose series whatever the starting age
InfluenzaInactivated, every year
Hepatitis B serology
ResultMeaning
Surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody all negativeSusceptible: vaccinate
Surface antibody onlyImmune from vaccination
Surface antibody and core antibody, no surface antigenImmune from natural infection (recovered)
Surface antigen with IgM (immunoglobulin M) core antibodyAcute infection
Surface antigen with IgG (immunoglobulin G) core antibody, no surface antibodyChronic infection
Pause point
HIV, CD4 count 320, no varicella immunity Offered as withhold it for HIV or immune globulin instead Is the vaccine live, and is the CD4 count 200 or higher? → Give the varicella vaccine; HIV alone does not bar every live vaccine
CD4 count 90, asks for a shingles vaccine Offered as defer it or the live zoster vaccine Is this vaccine live? → Recombinant zoster: not live, given at any CD4 count
Cirrhosis with an enlarged, congested spleen Offered as meningococcal or Hib Is the spleen absent, or only congested? → Congested is not absent: give the cirrhosis list, pneumococcal and hepatitis A and B
Practice
  1. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care CD4 count 320/mm³ on antiretroviral therapy varicella antibody negative No history of chickenpox or varicella vaccination T 36.8 °C · BP 118/74 mm Hg → Give the varicella vaccine → varicella is permitted once the CD4 count is 200 or above; HIV alone does not exclude every live vaccine
  2. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care CD4 count 120/mm³ measles antibody negative Started antiretroviral therapy 1 month ago T 36.9 °C · BP 120/76 mm Hg → Withhold MMR until CD4 is at least 200 and 15% for 6 months → MMR is live: contraindicated under a CD4 count of 200; given once the count is 200 or higher, with a CD4 percentage of 15% or higher, for at least 6 months
  3. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care in influenza season CD4 count 450/mm³ asks for the nasal spray vaccine Takes antiretroviral therapy daily T 37.0 °C · BP 122/78 mm Hg → Inactivated influenza vaccine → the live attenuated influenza vaccine is never given in HIV, at any CD4 count: use inactivated influenza, annually
  4. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care CD4 count 400/mm³ on antiretroviral therapy traveling to a yellow fever zone next month Never vaccinated against yellow fever T 36.7 °C · BP 116/72 mm Hg → Give yellow fever vaccine with caution → a CD4 count of 200 or higher permits yellow fever vaccine, with caution
  5. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care asks about pneumococcal vaccination CD4 count 160/mm³ Has never received a pneumococcal vaccine T 36.8 °C · BP 124/80 mm Hg → Give pneumococcal vaccine regardless of CD4 count → pneumococcal vaccine is not live: in HIV it is given regardless of age and CD4 count
  6. 30-year-old man with HIV comes to the clinic for routine care asks about shingles vaccination CD4 count 90/mm³ Had chickenpox as a child T 36.9 °C · BP 118/76 mm Hg → Recombinant zoster vaccine → recombinant zoster is not live, so it is permitted even at a low CD4 count, from age 19 in HIV rather than waiting until 50
  7. 36-year-old man with HIV comes for a vaccine review hepatitis B surface antigen negative core antibody negative; surface antibody positive Completed a hepatitis B vaccine series years ago CD4 count 450/mm³ · Afebrile → No hepatitis B vaccination needed → surface antibody alone, with negative surface antigen and core antibody, is immunity from vaccination
  8. 48-year-old man with cirrhosis from alcohol use comes for a checkup no vaccine records ascites controlled on diuretics Not immune to hepatitis A or B albumin 3.0 g/dL · platelets 98,000/mm³ → Pneumococcal, hepatitis A and hepatitis B → cirrhosis loses opsonins (the liver makes complement) and hepatitis A on a cirrhotic liver is fulminant: pneumococcal, hepatitis A and B
  9. 48-year-old man is seen 2 weeks after a splenectomy spleen removed after a car crash recovering well Vaccine records are up to date for his age T 36.8 °C · platelets 520,000/mm³ → Pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib → without a spleen the filter is lost and encapsulated organisms need splenic clearance: pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib
  10. 48-year-old man is about to start eculizumab blocks the terminal complement pathway no prior meningococcal vaccine Vaccine records otherwise up to date T 36.9 °C · BP 122/78 mm Hg · hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL → Meningococcal vaccination is mandatory → complement components 5 through 9 kill Neisseria: blocking them makes meningococcal vaccination mandatory
  11. 48-year-old man is scheduled to receive a cochlear implant for profound hearing loss no prior pneumococcal vaccine Vaccine records otherwise up to date T 36.7 °C · BP 124/80 mm Hg → Pneumococcal vaccination → a cochlear implant, like a cerebrospinal fluid leak, gives direct meningeal access: pneumococcal vaccination
  12. 26-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation asks which vaccines she needs it is influenza season not immune to rubella Last tetanus booster 3 years ago BP 112/70 mm Hg · Afebrile → Tdap and inactivated influenza → Tdap in every pregnancy (27 to 36 weeks) and inactivated influenza; no live vaccines in pregnancy (MMR, varicella, LAIV)
